[← Back to the lesson: Entropy: uncertainty over the next token](../entropy.qmd)

## Check your understanding

[Extended exercises on this topic](../en/exercises.qmd#foundations).

1. Does low entropy guarantee that the most likely token is correct?
2. How does entropy differ from the surprisal of the observed token?
3. Why must the tokenizer and token-counting convention be specified when comparing perplexity?

<details>
<summary>Show answers</summary>

1. No. Entropy describes the spread of the distribution, not factual correctness.
2. Entropy averages surprisal over all possible tokens under the predicted distribution; observed-token surprisal uses the probability assigned to the actual target.
3. Tokenizers segment text differently, changing the units and positions over which the average is computed.

</details>
